text: A room full of equipment. A day full of possibilities! Let's organize the details, and see the laboratory more clearly.
Meet Lab Tracker! Keep maintenance in view, with equipment and work records together in one focused, practical workspace.
Ready to move forward? Connect the assets, the spaces, and the people behind the work. That's where clearer administration begins.
Here's the big picture. Equipment has its own space, with identification, laboratory assignment, and status presented together in clear rows.
Need to review a repair? Maintenance sits right in the navigation. Find the records that describe the issue and its context.
Laboratories, categories, and accounts complete the workspace. The main areas of daily administration share a consistent place to get things done.
Start with the asset tag. Every item has an identity you can recognize, giving you a practical place to begin.
Then check the category. Item details and shared labels help describe what you're looking at, in one easy-to-scan row.
See the laboratory assignment alongside its status. Review the equipment in the context of the physical space where it belongs.
Let's add the details! Brand and model make the equipment record more useful, helping distinguish one item from the next.
Capture the serial number. Alongside the asset tag, it adds another point of identification beyond a general item description.
Record the date acquired. Add a category, a laboratory, and useful notes. A little context now makes a stronger record later.
Looking for something specific? Start with search. The equipment screen provides controls for tags, brands, models, and serial numbers.
Choose your filters! Narrow the view by laboratory, category, or status, and focus on the inventory you want to review.
Review the results, open the available item actions, or reset for a wider look. Your collection, with a more focused view.
Bring the issue into focus. Maintenance records connect a reported problem to the equipment it concerns. Keep the context together.
Check the status! Open work appears alongside the maintenance type and issue description, giving follow-up tasks a visible place.
Review the reported date, completion information, and cost. Together, those details make the maintenance entry more useful at the next review.
Report the issue. Choose the equipment, describe the task, and capture when it was reported. Start with the details that matter.
Record the work! Choose a type and status. Completion information, cost, and technician notes give you room for more context.
Keep that context close. An item-linked maintenance record gives practical details a clear home, ready for the next follow-up.
Give every laboratory a name. Make each space identifiable, with its details alongside the rest of your equipment management workspace.
Add the location. Connect the record to a physical space, and describe where that laboratory belongs within the organization.
Review the equipment count shown for each laboratory. Name, location, and assigned items bring your spaces and inventory together.
Monitors have their own category. A familiar part of the laboratory, with a shared label that makes the structure visible.
Motherboards have their place, too. Equipment counts appear beside the names, helping describe how the collection is grouped.
Keyboards and mice complete the picture here. Consistent categories give equipment a common language, alongside the laboratories that give it a place.
People keep the records moving! The accounts screen presents identity and username together, with a clear row for each user.
Review the role. The same straightforward table format keeps the experience consistent as you move between areas of the workspace.
Check account status and last login information, with available actions alongside. The people behind the work have an organized place, too.
Identify. Start with equipment and its useful details. Asset tags, models, and serial numbers give the collection a practical structure.
Organize. Connect items to laboratories and categories. Those shared labels and assignments make the inventory easier to describe and review.
Maintain. Bring issues and work details back to the equipment. Three connected steps, and a clearer rhythm for everyday administration.
Know your equipment! From an asset's identity to the laboratory where it belongs, keep the important details together in one workspace.
Keep maintenance moving. Record the issue, capture the context, and make the practical details ready for review. Build clarity through consistent records.
Choose clarity! Equipment, spaces, maintenance, and people, brought together. That's Lab Tracker. A more organized way to keep your laboratory moving forward!
